basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'In articulo diei illius ingressus est Noe et Sem et Cham et Japhet, filii ejus, et uxor'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: In articulo diei illius ingressus est Noe et Sem et Cham et Japhet, filii ejus, et uxor ejus, et tres uxores filiorum ejus cum eis in arcam. Ipsi et omne animal secundum genus suum, et caetera usque dum ait: omnesque volucres ingressae sunt ad Noe in arcam. Cuncta ergo animantia uno eodemque die ingressa sunt in arcam, quia non Noe laboravit ea multo labore ac longo tempore colligere atque introducere vel minare in arcam; sed divino nutu coacta, sponte cuncta veniebant in suo quaeque numero, praecedente illo cum liberis suis et uxoribus, sequebantur ex ordine, ac suas singula mansiunculas, Domino agente, quasi propria sponte subibant. Ad hoc enim valet quod dicitur de avibus, ingressae sunt ad Noe in arcam, et supra generaliter, et ex omni quod movetur super terram duo et duo ingressa sunt ad Noe in arcam. Eodem quoque die, id est, septimo decimo mensis secundi factum est quod sequitur.
